items.titulo: Code-driven AI illustrations are more useful than images from dedicated image models
items.resumen: An interesting trend in frontier LLMs released in the second half of 2026 is that they tend to be much better at visual reasoning and creative "design" than their predecessors. If you ask these text-output models to create a 2D image (or a 3D model, as discussed here previously ), you're very likely to get a useful result, and you may even get one that's aesthetically impressive. Release: datasette-charts 0.4a0 The new datasette-charts plugin has its own plugin hook to allow other plugins to define new chart types, but I hadn't actually used it for anything yet. I had Claude Opus 5.5 build an experimental plugins just to try out the hook and it came up with a bunch of friction points in the design. This release addresses those, which should make building additional chart plugins a whole lot more ergonomic. I've also added a website for the plugin, at charts.datasette.io

items.titulo: Inside the AI Training Data Market — Gabe Greenberg, G2i
items.resumen: A frontier lab can pay more for training data it gets to keep exclusive, or take a discount on data another lab can buy too. At AI Engineer CODE, G2i founder Gabe Greenberg tells swyx how labs make that decision, how small pilot orders turn into bigger...

items.titulo: Ant Group Releases LingSante-3.1-flash: An Open-Weight MoE Model with 560B Total Parameters and 25B Activations per Token
items.resumen: Ant Group's Afu team open-sourced LingSante-3.1-flash, a 560B-parameter MoE medical AI model with 25B active parameters, a 1M-token context and an MIT license. It ranks first among open models on InclusionMed. The post Ant Group Releases LingSante-3.1-flash: An Open-Weight MoE Model with 560B Total Parameters and 25B Activations per Token appeared first on MarkTechPost .
